transcript.text: Could you describe the challenges you faced while leading the migration of the settlement service from a monolith to three services?

I've spent six years as a software engineer, the last three at a payments company in Bengaluru. My biggest piece of work was splitting our settlement service out of the monolith into three services. I wrote the design document, got sign-off from two other teams and ran the cut-over over four weekends. On-call pages dropped from roughly 30 a month to 8. I'm applying now because the decisions I find most interesting, such as what to build and for which merchants, are made one level above me, and I want the business training to make them well.
How did this migration impact the team’s operational efficiency and service reliability?
transcript.anchor_quote: On-call pages dropped from roughly 30 a month to 8

transcript.text: I can't share the transaction volumes or revenue numbers; they're confidential to the company. What I can say is that settlement runs every night for all of our merchants, so an outage there is visible to customers the next morning.
Can you explain the key technical decisions and architectural patterns that you used to split the settlement service into three separate services?

feedback.summary: The candidate demonstrated clear personal ownership in leading a significant technical migration and provided evidence of impactful outcomes through reduced on-call pages. They showed awareness of the leadership nuances in managing a small team without formal authority. However, the session ended prematurely, limiting exploration into motivations, learning from setbacks, and contributions beyond technical delivery. The candidate also introduced an unrelated question mid-interview, which disrupted flow.

strengths.quote: I wrote the design document, got sign-off from two other teams and ran the cut-over over four weekends. On-call pages dropped from roughly 30 a month to 8
strengths.observation: Shows personal ownership and substantiated outcomes for a complex migration project.

strengths.quote: Actually, I managed the whole team for that migration. Well, not formally. There were three of us and I was the one who wrote the plan, but I didn't have anyone reporting to me
strengths.observation: Demonstrates leadership through influence without formal authority.

improvements.quote: I can't share the transaction volumes or revenue numbers; they're confidential to the company. What I can say is that settlement runs every night for all of our merchants, so an outage there is visible to customers the next morning
improvements.observation: Did not quantify or fully explain the operational benefits beyond call reductions, limiting assessment of impact.
improvements.suggestion: Practice articulating the impact of technical work in business terms without breaching confidentiality, such as describing improvements in uptime, customer experience, or team efficiency.

improvements.quote: By the way, do you know whether the ISB hostel allows cooking? I'm vegetarian and I was wondering about the mess food
improvements.observation: Introduced an unrelated logistical question during the interview, interrupting focus and flow.
improvements.suggestion: Work on maintaining interview focus and saving logistical or administrative queries for after the formal session.

improvements.quote: Can we stop here? I'd like to end the practice session now and look at the feedback
improvements.observation: Ended the session early, foregoing discussion on motivation, behavior, and future goals which are key for balanced evaluation.
improvements.suggestion: In future practice interviews, attempt to complete at least a full round of diverse topics to enable a comprehensive feedback experience.

feedback.next_exercise: Describe a project where you influenced peers without formal authority, specifically outlining the challenges, your approach to collaboration, the trade-offs you considered, and the outcome, all within 60 seconds.
